title: US Sales Hiring Index, October 2026: Fewer Companies Hiring, Not Smaller Sales Teams
summary: Sales hiring statistics, October 2026: the US Sales Hiring Index reads 93.3 as 7.7% fewer companies hired sales roles.
body_markdown:
(-14.3%) postings fell hardest; Account Management held flat (-0.2%).The US Sales Hiring Index reads **93.3** for the four weeks from August 17 to September 13, 2026, against a baseline of 100, which means US B2B sales hiring contracted month over month. New B2B sales postings fell 5.6%, but the number of companies hiring for sales fell faster, 7.7%, while the companies still hiring posted slightly more roles each (4.85 per employer, up from 4.75). The pullback in these sales hiring statistics is fewer companies building sales teams, not smaller sales teams. The newest four weeks point to a rebound, a provisional reading of 115.2, which we treat as directional until the data settles.


If you sell to sales teams, or time outbound around who is building one, the national number is the least useful part of this report. Below: where the decline sat by role, company size, and industry; 20 companies whose sales hiring just jumped to several times their own average; why recent funding does not predict those jumps; and the data-quality check that decides which reading we publish.


**TLDR:**


- The US Sales Hiring Index reads 93.3 (baseline 100) for August 17 to September 13, 2026: new US B2B sales postings fell 5.6% to 115,996, and distinct hiring employers fell 7.7% to 23,904.
- The decline is breadth, not intensity: companies still hiring posted 4.85 sales roles each, up from 4.75, while companies with 11-50 employees lost 19.8% of their hiring employers and employers with 1,001+ staff added hirers.
- Partnerships/Channel (-17.9%) and Sales Leadership >


- Recent funding does not predict sales-hiring surges: 2.9% of companies with a Sales hiring surge had a financing event in the prior 18 months, versus 3.6% of all companies hiring sales roles, a 0.81x ratio.
- The index is built from PredictLeads Job Openings data (279.2M+ postings since 2018 across 2.9M+ company websites), counted only after duplicate and job-board listings are filtered out; the newest four weeks read a provisional 115.2.


Source: PredictLeads Job Openings data, US B2B sales-role postings. Baseline: July 20 to August 16, 2026.


## What the US Sales Hiring Index measures


The US Sales Hiring Index is a monthly measure of how much, and how broadly, US companies are hiring for B2B sales roles, built from newly observed job postings in PredictLeads Job Openings data. It blends two ratios with equal weight: total new B2B sales postings against a baseline period (scale), and the number of distinct companies posting at least one such role against the same baseline (breadth).


**Index** = 100 x \[0.5 x (postings / baseline postings) + 0.5 x (hiring companies / baseline hiring companies)\]


The baseline is July 20 to August 16, 2026, the first four-week period we could confirm sits in a stable, comparable data-classification regime. One index point equals roughly a 1% change in the blended measure. We blend the two because each fails alone: a postings count can be moved by a few large employers, while a breadth count shows whether demand is spreading or narrowing. As a sensitivity check, the scale-only and breadth-only versions read 94.4 and 92.3 this month, so the weighting does not change the conclusion.


The index counts job postings, not hires or headcount. Government data answers a different question: the BLS[Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS)](https://www.bls.gov/jlt/) estimates openings by industry, not by role, so it cannot isolate sales hiring or name the companies doing it. For the mechanics of reading postings as a company-level signal, see our guide to[using job openings data as a company growth signal](https://predictleads.com/blog/job-openings-data-company-growth/) . Every PredictLeads posting carries a` first_seen_at` timestamp, which is what lets the index count new postings by discovery date rather than open inventory.


## October 2026 reading: fewer companies hiring, not smaller sales teams


Between the baseline (July 20 to August 16) and the current period (August 17 to September 13, 2026), US B2B sales postings fell from 122,912 to 115,996, and distinct hiring employers fell from 25,901 to 23,904.

Breadth fell further than postings, so the decline came from companies leaving the hiring pool, not from hiring companies cutting requisitions. The companies that kept hiring posted slightly more roles each, 4.85 versus 4.75, which offset part of the breadth loss. If you sell into active sales teams, that is the read that matters: 1,997 fewer companies were building sales capacity this period, and the ones still building were not building less.


### Why we lead with 93.3, not the provisional 115.2


The most recent four weeks, September 14 to October 11, 2026, read 115.2: 140,263 postings from 30,096 employers. We do not lead with that number because the newest weeks of any snapshot have not finished duplicate and filtering. At the time of this snapshot, the share of those weeks’ postings flagged as duplicates, reposts, or job-board listings was still falling week over week, the pattern of a cohort that has not been fully processed. Under-filtered weeks can overstate counts until filtering catches up, which takes several weeks.


The settled, comparable reading is therefore 93.3. The 115.2 reading is directional: it suggests September hiring recovered, and we will confirm or revise it in the November edition. The rebound is also breadth-led (the employer-only index reads 116.2), so if it holds, it reverses the pattern above. Each Job Openings record keeps` first_seen_at` and` last_seen_at` , so any window can be rerun once it settles.


## Sales hiring statistics by role family


Every named sales role family posted fewer openings in the current period except Sales Enablement, which grew on a small base. Partnerships/Channel fell hardest (-17.9%), Sales Leadership second (-14.3%), and Account Management held flat (-0.2%).

### Where the closing and leadership roles went


Account Executive postings fell 10.4%, from 10,572 to 9,470, the largest absolute decline of any named family (1,102 postings). Sales Engineering and Solutions Consulting fell at a similar rate (-10.8%, 2,296 to 2,047). SDR/BDR postings fell a smaller 7.0% (6,767 to 6,294). A steeper drop in closing roles than in prospecting roles is consistent with companies slowing new-logo capacity first, though postings cannot show the motive.


Sales Leadership (Director, VP, and C-level) fell 14.3%, from 4,201 to 3,601. Fewer senior commercial searches is consistent with companies holding leadership hires while they set next year’s plans. Partnerships/Channel fell 17.9% (1,603 to 1,316), the steepest drop of any family with a meaningful base. It is also small enough that a handful of employers can move it.


### What held, and what to read with caution


Account Management barely moved (11,444 to 11,422), consistent with companies protecting existing-customer revenue while slowing new-logo hiring. Sales Ops/RevOps (499 to 485) and Sales Enablement (165 to 196) run on bases under 500 postings a month, so read their changes as directional, not as precise percentages.


About 70% of postings in both periods carry generic titles such as Sales Representative or Sales Manager that do not name a modern GTM subfunction. That bucket fell 4.9%, in the same direction as the named families, so the decline is not a classification artifact. In the provisional four weeks, every named family reads above its baseline, led by Account Management at 119.2 among families with a meaningful base; treat those readings as directional too.


Role families here come from title text. Every PredictLeads posting also carries a` seniority` level and an O*NET code in` onet_data` , and our walkthrough on[finding companies hiring for a specific role by O*NET code](https://predictleads.com/blog/find-companies-hiring-role-onet/) shows how to rebuild the same cut by occupation.


## Company size: the breadth loss sat in companies with 200 or fewer employees


Small companies drove the breadth decline, and large ones held steady. Companies with 200 or fewer employees account for 1,634 of the 1,997 fewer hiring employers, while the number of employers with 1,001+ staff hiring sales roles rose from 4,998 to 5,036.

They also hire at a different scale: 18.76 postings per hiring employer, against 2.46 at companies with 51-200 staff. The 51-200 band had the steepest posting decline of any size band (-21.4%), and the 11-50 band lost the largest share of its hiring employers (-19.8%).

Software Development had the sharpest breadth loss among the industries we break out: 1,563 companies posted B2B sales roles in the current period, down from 1,977 (-20.9%), and its postings fell 18.4%. Construction was the only one to grow in both postings (+3.7%) and hiring companies (+1.9%).

### Industries where a few employers move the number


Telecommunications postings fell 30.7% while hiring companies rose slightly (187 to 190), so the drop came from a few large employers posting fewer roles: postings per company fell from 16.83 to 11.48. Non-profit Organization Management posts 17 to 25 sales-category roles per hiring employer across all three periods, roughly 3.5 to 5 times the cross-industry average of 4.75 to 4.85. A small number of large organizations drive that industry’s totals, so read any industry-level claim about either one with that concentration in mind.


Retail remains the largest labeled industry (8,177 postings from 672 companies). Our title filter removes consumer roles such as Sales Associate and Store Manager, but some retailers post genuine wholesale, field, or B2B account roles, so we did not exclude companies by industry label alone. Some residual consumer-sales noise likely remains in that row. Biotechnology Research has no baseline row in this edition, so it shows no change. For the industries where overall hiring, not just sales hiring, is accelerating, see our[hiring momentum tracker](https://predictleads.com/blog/industries-accelerating-hiring-momentum/) .


## 20 companies behind the index: sales-hiring surges to watch


The national reading tells you the market’s direction; the company-level changes tell you where to look. To find them, we started with the 20,699 companies that carried a validated Sales-department hiring-surge flag in PredictLeads data over the trailing 90 days as of October 23, 2026. A surge means a company’s recent sales postings jumped well above its own prior 12-month monthly average. We removed consumer-retail and clearly non-B2B employers, then selected 20 that show unusual acceleration, a sales function appearing from near zero, or a market entry. This is a curated list, not a ranking by size.


Read them with three cautions. First, a surge is an observable change in hiring allocation, not a confirmed contract, raise, or launch; every interpretation below is a hypothesis to check. Second, the 30-day counts end on the signal dates (October 13 to 16, 2026), so they sit in the provisional window, not the settled period behind the 93.3 reading. Third, several multiples rest on single-digit counts: 4 postings against a 0.1 monthly average reads as 40x, which is a real change but a small one.


### Step-changes from a near-zero base


- **Benev Company** (Pharmaceutical Manufacturing, 51-200 employees): 29 sales postings in 30 days against a 0.7 monthly average, 41.4x. A step-change this size is consistent with a territory or distributor-network launch, which no public labor statistic would show.
- **MDT** (IT Services and IT Consulting, 51-200): 4 postings against 0.1, 40x. A sales function appearing from almost nothing.
- **Mygrant Glass Company** (Glass, Ceramics and Concrete Manufacturing, 1,001-5,000): 7 against 0.2, 35x. An established auto-glass wholesale distributor that rarely hires sales reps; consistent with a distribution-network expansion.
- **Watchtower Security** (Security Systems Services, 51-200): 4 against 0.2, 20x, a security-systems integrator building sales capacity from near zero.
- **US Air Conditioning Distributors** (Wholesale, 201-500): 7 against 0.4, 17.5x, the kind of account or territory build-out that can precede a new product line or region.
- **Horvath & Partners Management Consulting** (Business Consulting and Services, 1,001-5,000): 12 against 0.8, 15x, business-development capacity well beyond its own history.
- **Amplix** (IT Services and IT Consulting, 51-200) and **Carr, Riggs & Ingram** (Business Consulting and Services, 1,001-5,000): 4 postings each against 0.3, about 13x. Professional-services firms formalizing a sales motion are a less obvious signal worth tracking.


### Large absolute build-outs


- **Craig Technical Consulting** (Defense and Space Manufacturing, 201-500): 75 sales postings in 30 days against a 6.2 monthly average, 12.1x, the largest absolute count on the list. A build-out this fast is consistent with a new contract that needs program and account-management capacity, though postings alone cannot confirm one.
- **ClearPay Processing** (Financial Services, 11-50): 41 postings against 13.6, 3.0x, an already elevated pace that tripled again.
- **Gondola** (Technology, Information and Media, 2-10): 30 postings against 8.4, 3.6x.


Check the last two before you act. A company listed at 2-10 or 11-50 employees that averages 8 to 14 sales postings a month is posting faster than its listed headcount can easily absorb. That can mean a stale size band, commission-only or contract roles, or one role posted across many locations. It is still a signal, but verify the role type before you treat it as a headcount build-out.


### Software and IT vendors scaling go-to-market


- **Wisetail** (Software Development, 51-200): 5 against 0.7, 7x, a learning-management software vendor stepping up from a very low base.
- **Vertosoft** (IT Services and IT Consulting, 51-200): 5 against 0.9, 5.5x, consistent with a new vendor line or channel push.
- **Dotmatics** (Software Development, 501-1,000): 8 against 1.6, 5x, a scientific R&D software vendor expanding its commercial team.
- **AutoCash** (Technology, Information and Internet, 11-50): 6 against 1.2, 5x.
- **Techsalerator** (Information Services, 51-200): 3 against 0.7, 4.3x, small in absolute terms but notable against its own base.
- **ISpeedToLead** (Software Development, 51-200): 7 against 2.0, 3.5x. A sales-tooling vendor whose customers are other sales teams, which makes it worth watching as an early read on demand.
- **Vcluster** (Software Development, 51-200): 6 against 1.9, 3.2x, a Kubernetes infrastructure vendor tripling sales hiring.


### Market entry and indirect demand


- **Pexon Consulting** (IT Services and IT Consulting, 51-200): 3 postings against 0.6, 5x. A European IT consultancy posting US sales roles reads as a US market-entry signal, not routine domestic hiring.
- **Cross Country Search** (Hospitals and Health Care, 1,001-5,000): 6 against 1.7, 3.5x. A healthcare placement firm scaling its own sales team may reflect demand from the hospital systems it serves; treat that as a hypothesis.

## Does recent funding predict a sales-hiring surge? Not in this data


No. Of the 20,699 companies with a Sales-department hiring-surge flag in the trailing 90 days, 604 (2.9%) had a financing event in the 18 months before the surge. In a control group of every company that posted at least one US B2B sales role in the current period, surging or not, 863 of 23,904 (3.6%) had a financing event in the trailing 18 months.


Source: PredictLeads data. The groups overlap and use different windows; see methodology.


That is a ratio of 0.81x: surging companies were no more likely, and slightly less likely, to have raised recently than ordinary sales-hiring companies. We would not read the gap itself as meaningful, because the two groups use different windows and partly overlap. The finding is the absence of a positive lift.


Financing Events capture announced rounds, so revenue-funded or budget-cycle hiring never shows up in this test, and that is the point: most sales-hiring surges happen without a funding headline. The data does not tell you what drives them. It does tell you not to gate a hiring-surge play on a funding announcement. PredictLeads Financing Events covers 210,800+ funding events since 2016, and if you do time outreach around rounds, our guide to[timing outreach by funding stage](https://predictleads.com/blog/time-outreach-by-funding-stage/) shows where it helps.


## What GTM teams should do with the October reading


None of these are purchase predictions. They are ways to act on the reading without overreading it.


- **Filter on breadth, not the headline.** The 23,904 employers that posted a US B2B sales role this period are the accounts still committing sales budget. Re-score target accounts each month on whether they posted one; our guide to[prioritizing accounts with hiring signals](https://predictleads.com/blog/hiring-signals-b2b-sales-account-prioritization/) shows a scoring setup.
- **Refresh small-company lists more often.** Companies with 11-50 employees lost 19.8% of their hiring employers in four weeks, so an SMB list built on last quarter’s hiring signals decays fast.
- **Lean on enterprise for stability.** Employers with 1,001+ staff hiring sales roles rose from 4,998 to 5,036 while the wider market contracted.
- **Sell to leaders already in their seats.** Sales Leadership postings fell 14.3%, so fewer new sales leaders are arriving with fresh mandates this quarter.
- **Do not wait for a funding round.** With a 0.81x funding ratio, a sales-hiring surge is a signal on its own terms.
- **Flag first-time functions.** A company posting Sales Engineering or RevOps roles for the first time can be standing up a motion that did not exist before, which is worth routing to competitive-intelligence and enablement teams even at low volume.


## Methodology and limitations


### Population and role taxonomy


Source: PredictLeads Job Openings, joined to company attributes (LinkedIn employee-size band and LinkedIn industry). Population: newly observed US job postings, resolved to a US state or to “United States,” tagged with the sales job category. A title-level B2B filter excludes titles that match retail, consumer, banking, or generic customer-service patterns (for example Sales Associate, Store Manager, Personal Banker, and Customer Service Representative), a rule validated against a manual sample of the remaining population.


Remaining titles are classified into role families by title text, with an “other/generic” catch-all. The Sales Leadership family uses PredictLeads seniority levels (Director, VP, C-level, President, Head). The metric is newly observed postings by first-discovery date, not active inventory: we tested open-inventory counts and found the closure signal more exposed to the processing lag described below.


### Index windows


Baseline: July 20 to August 16, 2026. Current (settled): August 17 to September 13, 2026. Provisional: September 14 to October 11, 2026. Hiring-company counts are distinct employers, summed across company-size bands. The formula and sensitivity check are in the first section above.


### The data-quality finding behind the baseline


While validating completeness, we found that the share of discovered US postings that PredictLeads excludes as duplicates, reposts, or job-board listings rose from a 2025 norm of about 28% to 32% (July 21 to October 6, 2025) to a peak of about 50% to 52% in the weeks of June 15 to June 29, 2026, before settling. It measured 36.4% in the baseline window and 37.8% in the current window. Raw discovery volume, before any filtering, held between about 650,000 and 1.2 million postings a week from July 2025 to October 2026 with no sustained decline, so this was a filtering change, not a coverage loss.


Because filtered counts from the elevated period are not comparable with counts on either side of it, we build no comparison across it, and the baseline starts after it. The same check is why the newest four weeks are provisional: duplicate detection takes several weeks to mature for each cohort of postings.


### Hiring surges and the funding cross-check


The watchlist and the funding test use a company-level Sales-department hiring-surge flag: a company’s recent sales postings measured against its own prior 12-month monthly average. The funding test compares companies flagged in the trailing 90 days (as of October 23, 2026) with all companies posting at least one US B2B sales role in the current period, checking each for a Financing Events record in the trailing 18 months. The groups overlap and use different windows, and we report the ratio rather than a statistical test, so read it as an absence of lift, not a measured negative effect.


### What this index does not claim, and revisions


Hiring is an observable allocation signal, not proof of a purchase, financing event, or business outcome. Phrases such as “consistent with” are deliberate; we do not claim intent or causation from hiring data alone. Postings measure hiring intent, not hires.


The index updates monthly, with windows rolling forward once each month’s data has matured, roughly four to six weeks after discovery, so expect the provisional reading to be revised. This URL previously carried our September 2026 sales and RevOps hiring statistics, built on 30-day windows from July 8 to September 5, 2026 and a different sales population. Part of that comparison falls before the July 20, 2026 baseline start described above, so the September figures are superseded and are not comparable with this edition.

## Final thoughts on US sales hiring in October 2026


The October reading says US B2B sales hiring contracted in breadth: 1,997 fewer companies posted a sales role, most of them companies with 200 or fewer employees, while the companies still hiring, enterprises in particular, held their pace. The newest weeks suggest a September rebound that the November edition will confirm or revise. ## Frequently Asked Questions


**Is US sales hiring slowing down in 2026?**
Yes, on the settled data. The US Sales Hiring Index reads 93.3 for August 17 to September 13, 2026 (baseline 100): new US B2B sales postings fell 5.6% to 115,996, and distinct hiring employers fell 7.7% to 23,904. The decline came from fewer companies hiring, mostly companies with 200 or fewer employees, while companies still hiring posted slightly more roles each. The newest four weeks read a provisional 115.2, which suggests a September rebound the next edition will confirm or revise.


**What is the US Sales Hiring Index?**
The US Sales Hiring Index is a monthly PredictLeads measure of US B2B sales hiring that blends scale (new sales postings) and breadth (distinct companies hiring) against a baseline of 100. The baseline is July 20 to August 16, 2026. It counts newly observed postings after removing duplicates, job-board listings, and retail, banking, and customer-service titles. It is built from PredictLeads Job Openings, which holds 279.2M+ postings since 2018.


**Why is the latest sales hiring reading of 115.2 only provisional?**
Because the newest weeks of any snapshot have not finished duplicate and job-board filtering. At the time of this snapshot, the share of those weeks’ postings flagged as duplicates or job-board listings was still falling week over week, the pattern of a cohort that has not been fully processed, and under-filtered weeks can overstate counts. The settled, comparable reading is 93.3. The 115.2 reading will be confirmed or revised in the next edition.


**Do companies hire more salespeople after raising funding?**
Not in this data. Of 20,699 companies with a Sales-department hiring surge in the trailing 90 days, 2.9% had a financing event in the prior 18 months, versus 3.6% of all 23,904 companies posting a US B2B sales role, a ratio of 0.81x. The groups overlap and use different windows, so the result shows no positive lift rather than a negative effect. PredictLeads Financing Events covers 210,800+ funding events since 2016 if you want to run the same test on your own accounts.


**Which sales roles are companies cutting back on in 2026?**
Partnerships/Channel (-17.9%, 1,603 to 1,316 postings) and Sales Leadership (-14.3%, 4,201 to 3,601) fell hardest between the July 20 to August 16 and August 17 to September 13, 2026 periods. Sales Engineering (-10.8%) and Account Executive (-10.4%) followed, while SDR/BDR fell 7.0% and Account Management held flat at -0.2%. Sales Enablement rose 18.8%, on a base too small to read as precise. Role families come from job titles in PredictLeads Job Openings data, and each posting also carries a seniority level.
